terms.grammar: plural of omnis, used as a pronoun
evidence: Ter. And. 309: facile omnēs, cum valēmus, rēcta cōnsilia aegrōtīs damus
Plin. Ep. 9.33.5: serpit per colōniam fāma; concurrere omnēs
terms.comment: Latin says “all”, in the plural, as with omnia, everything. All together, as one body, is ūniversī or cūnctī; everyone else, cēterī.

terms.gloss: each one, everyone (taken one by one)
terms.grammar: pronoun, usually after a reflexive, a relative or a superlative
evidence: Cic. Amic. 62: caprās et ovēs quot quisque habēret, dīcere posse
terms.comment: “Each his own”: suus cuique; optimus quisque, all the best people (Lewis & Short).

evidence: Cic. Amic. 99: apertē enim adūlantem nēmō nōn videt
Sen. Ep. 86.14: quōrum nēmō nōn olīvētum alterī pōnit

phrases.latin: statim urceātim plovēbat … et omnēs rīdēbant ūdī tanquam mūrēs
phrases.english: at once it was raining buckets … and everyone laughed, wet as drowned rats

phrases.latin: Quot hominēs, tot sententiae; suus cuique mōs.
phrases.english: So many people, so many opinions; everyone has their own way.

phrases.latin: facile omnēs, cum valēmus, rēcta cōnsilia aegrōtīs damus
phrases.english: when we’re well, we all find it easy to give good advice to the sick
